rules.summary: Land-based fishers in the West Coast bioregion: combined bag limit of 2 demersal scalefish. Boat-based demersal fishing in the West Coast region is closed (boat fishing is outside this app's scope). Check DPIRD for the full list of demersal species and size limits.

rules.summary: South Coast bioregion (from 1 June 2026): mixed demersal scalefish bag limit of 4 per person, including no more than 1 WA dhufish, 1 western blue groper and 2 pink snapper. Pink snapper minimum size 450 mm.
rules.source_name: DPIRD — New statewide finfish size and bag limits from 1 June 2026

rules.summary: Black stingray and smooth stingray are recreationally protected in the West Coast and South Coast bioregions — they must not be taken. Any protected species caught must be returned to the water immediately.

guide.title: Licences
guide.text: You don't need a licence to fish from the shore. Exceptions: rock lobster, abalone, marron, south-west freshwater angling and net fishing need licences. Any fishing from a powered boat (including spearfishing) needs a Recreational Fishing from Boat Licence.

guide.title: Lines, hooks & baits
guide.text: From the shore you may use up to 2 lines, and rods/lines must be attended. In the West Coast bioregion, when fishing for demersal scalefish, only 1 bait or lure per line. Elsewhere (and for other fish) up to 3 baits or lures per line. Bait jigs with more than 3 hooks are illegal in WA.

guide.title: Spearfishing
guide.text: Spearfishing is allowed in most ocean waters, except some marine protected areas (sanctuary zones) and around dive wrecks. Rivers, tributaries and dams are closed to spearfishing (a hand spear may be used for estuarine cobbler in estuaries). Land-based spearfishing for WA dhufish is not permitted. Protected species (e.g. grey nurse shark, seadragons) must never be speared. Dive with a buddy, use a dive flag and consider a shark deterrent.

guide.title: Measuring
guide.text: Measure finfish from the tip of the snout to the tip of the tail.

guide.title: Possession limits
guide.text: Away from home you may hold: 10 kg of fillets plus 10 kg of large pelagic fillets (skin on), or 10 kg of fillets plus one day's bag limit of whole fish, or 2 days' bag limit of whole fish. At your home: up to 20 kg of fillets.

guide.title: Filleting & landing
guide.text: Fish carried at sea and landed must have skin attached so they can be identified (whole, gutted and gilled, trunks or skin-on fillets). Two fillets count as one fish for bag limits.

guide.title: Sharks & rays
guide.text: Sharks and rays: combined bag limit of 3 per day. Black stingray and smooth stingray are protected in the West Coast and South Coast bioregions — release them.

guide.title: West Coast bioregion (Perth → Augusta)
guide.text: Boat fishing for demersal scalefish is closed until Spring 2027. Land-based fishers can still catch demersal scalefish by line or spear (outside spawning closures), with a mixed demersal bag of 2 per person — but WA dhufish can't be speared from land. Pink snapper minimum 500 mm between Lancelin and Black Point.

guide.title: South Coast bioregion (Denmark → Esperance)
guide.text: From 1 June 2026: mixed demersal bag of 4 per person, including no more than 1 WA dhufish, 1 western blue groper and 2 pink snapper (minimum 450 mm). Bight redfish, yelloweye redfish and swallowtail: 4 of each plus a mixed bag of 4 other demersals.

guide.title: Crabs
guide.text: Take crabs by hand, blunt wire hook, drop net (max 1.5 m across, max 10 per person) or rigid scoop net. Blue swimmer crab: minimum 127 mm carapace width, bag 20. Mud crab: bag 5. Release berried (egg-carrying) and undersize crabs immediately.

guide.title: Rock lobster
guide.text: Needs a rock lobster licence. Bag 8 per fisher per day; possession limit 24 per person.
